title: DPP EPCIS import record, version 2
description: The durable record of one retained EPCIS source under the epcis-json@1 profile (spec/epcis-interoperability.md section 2): what was received, where its exact bytes are kept, which request it answers and how a repeat of that request is recognised, how it was interpreted, what each event's validation and mapping found, how each event arrived against what its source already held, what was published from it under separate authority, and how far a pull got. Operational state never substitutes for a verification report, no field of this record is a token operation, and nothing in it says who made the document or that its events happened. Version 1 is epcis-import-v1.schema.json beside it, for records stored under that version.

importId.description: The stable internal identity of this import.

requestId.description: The caller's idempotency key, bound to requestDigest: an identical retry resumes or returns this import, a reuse with different bytes is a conflict.

requestDigest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical request the idempotency key is bound to. For a file import it is taken over the RFC 8785 form of an object with exactly the members byteLength, mediaType, sha256 and sourceId, as this record carries them. Receipt time, provenance and policy are not part of it.

idempotency.description: How a repeat of requestId is recognised, stated so that a reader of the record alone can tell.

scope.description: Where requestId is unique. source: within this record's sourceId in one store, so the same requestId under another sourceId is another request. store: across every source of one store.

rule.description: A request under a held requestId is the same request exactly when its requestDigest equals the held one. Any other is a conflict, and the held import stands.

sourceId.description: The configured source identity events are scoped under. It names a configured origin, never an account type.

sha256.description: The digest of the exact received bytes; export returns bytes with this digest or nothing.

bytesRef.description: Where the exact bytes are retained: a store key, a path or a content address, as the deployment names it.

sourceLocation.description: Provenance, never authentication proof. Credentials are never recorded here.

origin.description: The configured repository origin a query was made to, without credentials.

query.description: The standard query parameters used, by name.

filename.description: The name a file arrived under. A name, never an address, a query or a credential.

contextRefs.description: The context declarations of the source exactly as found, each with its pinned digest or the statement that it is unpinned.

scope.description: document, or the pointer of the event that declared it.

profileRefs.description: The interoperability and credential profiles this import was interpreted under: for example epcis-json@1 alone, or beside it epcis-vsc@1 or epcis-vsc@2 where one of the parked mapping profiles was selected.

policyId.description: The named operator policy the limits, source scope and any automation were read from.

limits.description: The limits in force for this import, as the profile discloses them.

state.description: received: the exact bytes and this record are durable and the arrival of each event is not yet recorded. evaluated: every event's validation, mapping and arrival are recorded, nothing is published and no arrival of this import is part of an open conflict. publication-pending: a separately authorised publication was requested and is unresolved. published: at least one event was published as a credential. blocked: a conflict or a refused publication needs explicit resolution. Never a verification verdict.

documentValidity.description: valid: the envelope is recognised, the pinned schema accepted the document, and no envelope, context or identifier check failed. invalid: the source parsed safely and is retained as evidence that was received; it is excluded from every result described as valid or conformant. Neither value says who made the document, that it is authentic, or that an event in it happened.

findings.description: Document-level findings: envelope, schema and context findings that are not about one event. An implementation MAY bound how many findings it records; when it does, it records a finding that says how many were made.

preservedExtensions.description: Members of the envelope the schema does not name, retained in the bytes and listed here.

checkpoint.description: The durable pull checkpoint (the next page token, or the record-time cutoff reached), written only after the page's imports and results are durable.

complete.description: True only when the source answered the whole bounded query without a next page and within the limits; never an assertion of complete history.

completenessLimits.description: Every reason the result is not complete history: the query scope, a page limit reached, an expired cursor, a timestamp-only bound.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the retained document; the empty pointer is a single event accepted as the whole source.

sourceOutcome.description: The outcome of reaching a source: no discovered EPCIS link; the source demanded authentication; the source refused this caller; the source did not answer or answered an error; the source answered a media type that is not EPCIS (an HTML login page with status 200 is this, never success); the bytes were refused before retention; the bounded query ended before the source did; or the bounded query completed. A successful query with zero matching events is ok with an empty event list, never any other outcome.

event.description: One event of the source. Three identifiers are kept apart and never relabelled: eventId is the event's own identifier as its source declared it, scoped to sourceId; a local identity is assigned at ingestion to an event that declares none; and neither is a GS1 CBV Event Hash ID, which this record does not carry.

eventId.description: The event's own eventID, exactly as declared, when it carries one. Recorded as written, whatever form it takes.

identity.description: The scoped identity duplicates and conflicts are decided under: the eventID, or the local identity.

identityKind.description: event-id: identity is the declared eventID. local: identity is the local ingestion identity. Arrivals are compared within one sourceId, one kind and one identity.

eventType.description: The event's type as declared; empty when the event names none.

bodyDigest.description: The canonical event-body digest: RFC 8785 over the event without recordTime and errorDeclaration plus the sorted context digests.

schema.description: Whether the pinned schema accepted the document this event belongs to; unknown when validation was not run.

resolution.description: resolved only when every corrective event named is held under this source; an EPCIS error declaration is never a VSC correction.

mapping.description: The event's outcome under the mapping profile named in profile, or not-attempted when the import selected no mapping profile, as an import under epcis-json@1 alone does. The epcis-vsc mapping profiles are parked, and an implementation that does not support them records not-attempted.

arrival.description: How this event relates to what the source already held under the same identity. new: nothing was held. duplicate: a held observation has this body, record time and error declaration. new-observation: a held observation has this body with another record time or error declaration. conflict: no held observation has this body. Absent while the import is received.

observation.description: The observation this arrival is: the one it added, or for a duplicate the held one it repeats.

sequence.description: The observation's position among those held under the identity.

conflict.description: Present when this arrival added an observation to an identity that holds more than one body; every body stays retained and visible. state is what held when this record was last written: the conflict is settled only while its latest decision covers every body held, so a body that arrives later reopens it.

conflictId.description: The identity of the conflict among the bodies held under this event's scoped identity.

resolutionId.description: The decision record that settled it.

resolution.description: What was decided, in the decider's words.

publication.description: The separately authorised publication of this event as a credential, if one was requested. The credential's bytes and identity are persisted before anchoring; a retry after an uncertain answer resumes this record and never issues again.

digest.description: The digest of the exact issued credential bytes.

operationId.description: The durable operation the publication runs under.

authorisedBy.description: The server-side authority that permitted publication; never a role the request body supplied.
